h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר ו׳ Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Vav

p: הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ וְגוֹמֵר לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא
"Behold, I send, etc., before the coming of the great and awesome day of Hashem"
(מַלְאָכִי ג', כ"ג).
(Malachi 3:23).
כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ שַׁבָּת הַקָּטָן מַלְכוּת, שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל בִּינָה,
Just as there is Shabbos HaKatan (Malchus) and Shabbos HaGadol (Binah),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּתִּיקּוּנִים
as brought in Tikkunei Zohar
תִּיקּוּן י"ט,
Tikkun 19,
כֵּן יֵשׁ יוֹם קָטָן וְיוֹם גָּדוֹל.
so too there is a "small day" and a "great day."
דְּשַׁבָּת הוּא סְתָם "יוֹם", דִּכְתִיב
For Shabbos is unqualified "Day," as it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית א', ה'):
(Bereishis 1:5):
וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם,
"And God called the light Day,"
וְזֶה הָאוֹר נִגְנַז, וְאִיתָא
and this light was hidden away, and it is stated
(בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר סִימָן ק"ס):
(in Sefer HaBahir, Section 160):
לָקַח שְׁבִיעִי וְשָׂם לָהֶם בִּמְקוֹמוֹ וְהַשְּׁאָר גְּנָזוֹ לַצַּדִּיקִים.
"He took the seventh and placed it for them in its stead, and the rest He hid away for the righteous."
וּבְשַׁבָּת שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר הָאוֹר נִקְרָא "יוֹם",
And on Shabbos, where the light remained, it is called "Day,"
וּשְׁאָר הַיָּמִים נִקְרָאִים יוֹם בְּהַשְׁאָלָה;
while the other days are called "day" only in a borrowed sense;
וְלָזֶה דָּרְשׁוּ
and for this reason they expounded
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"ה, י"ב וּבְשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים צ"ה):
(Shemos Rabbah 25:12 and Shocher Tov, Tehillim 95):
הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ
"Today (HaYom), if you would but heed His voice"
עַל הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא יוֹם הַמְּיוּחָד
referring to Shabbos, which is the unique Day
(תַּנְחוּמָא וַיֵּרָא א').
(Tanchuma Vayeira 1).
וְזֶה יוֹם קָטָן, דְּשַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת
And this is a "small day," for Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come—one-sixtieth of the World to Come, as they said in Berachos
וְיֵשׁ יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
And there are the Days of Mashiach, which are also a semblance of the World to Come,
אַךְ יוֹתֵר מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
yet a higher semblance of the World to Come,
שֶׁהֵם כְּבָר בְּתוֹסֶפֶת שַׁבָּת, יוֹם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ שַׁבָּת
for they are already in the extension of Shabbos, "a day that is entirely Shabbos"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר),
(as explained elsewhere),
וְזֶה יוֹם גָּדוֹל, אוֹר גָּדוֹל.
and this is a "great day," a great light.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' נ"ד.):
הִנֵּה יוֹם בָּא לַה'
"Behold, a day comes (ba) for Hashem"
הָכִי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: הִנֵּה יוֹם יָבוֹא וְכוּלֵּי.
it should have said, "Behold, a day will come (yavo)," etc.
רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר: תְּרֵין יוֹמִין אִינּוּן לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא:
Rabbi Yitzchak said: "There are two days to the Holy One, blessed is He:
חַד שָׁארֵי עִמֵּיהּ, מַלְכוּת
one that abides with Him—Malchus"
(הַיְינוּ יוֹם קָטָן),
(which is the small day),
וְחַד אָתֵי לְקַמֵּיהּ, בִּינָה
"and one that comes before Him—Binah"
(וְהַיְינוּ יוֹם גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא יְמוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ, וְהוּא קָרוֹב לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא שֶׁהוּא בִּינָה).
(which is the great day, the Days of Mashiach, which is close to the World to Come, which is Binah).
וְכַד הַאי יוֹמָא אָתֵי לְאַגָּחָא קְרָבָא,
And when this day comes to wage war
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּת זַיִ"ן, מָאן זַיִן, חֶרֶב לַה' מָלְאָה דָם
which is the attribute of Malchus, weapons (zayin), "the sword of Hashem is filled with blood"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' נ"ד.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 54a),
אַפְקִיד מַלְכָּא בִּידַהּ כָּל זַיְינִין דִּילֵיהּ
"the King entrusted into her hand all His weapons"
(שָׁם נ"א.)
(ibid. 51a)
וְכַד הַאי יוֹמָא אָתֵי לְאַגָּחָא קְרָבָא, אִזְדַּוּוּג בְּהַאי יוֹמָא אַחֲרָא בִּינָה דְּצֶדֶק.
when this day comes to wage war, it unites with that other day, Binah of righteousness.
מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא אִיהִי דִּינָא,
Holy Malchus is judgment,
וּבִינָה אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָאו אִיהִי דִּינָא, מִסִּטְרָאָה אִשְׁתְּכַח גְּבוּרָה,
and Binah, even though it is not judgment itself, from its side Gevurah is found,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
as brought in the holy Zohar
(שָׁם ס"ד סוֹף ע"א)
(ibid. 64, end of amud a)
דְּדִינִין מִתְּעָרִין מִינַּהּ,
that judgments are aroused from it;
וְזֶה שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
and this is what is brought in the holy Zohar:
וְנָטַל זַיְינִין עַל זַיְינֵיהּ וְאָגַח קְרָבָא בְּכוּלָּא וְכוּלֵּי.
"And it took weapons upon its weapons and waged war against all, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁבָּא מֵהַיִּרְאָה שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת מַלְכוּת
That is, just as there is repentance that comes from fear, which is the attribute of Malchus
אִיהִי יִרְאָה וְשַׁרְיָא בַּהּ יִרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
"She is fear and fear rests upon her," as brought in the holy Zohar
(הַקְדָּמָה ה':)
(Introduction 5b)
וְיֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה בִּינָה: וּלְבָבוֹ יָבִין וָשָׁב,
and there is supernal repentance, Binah—"and his heart will understand (yavin) and repent"
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מִיִּרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and it too comes from fear, as it is said
(Mishlei 2:5):
אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה'
"Then you will understand (tavin) the fear of Hashem"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
and as we have explained;
כֵּן יֵשׁ בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יוֹם קָטָן: מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, אוֹר קָטָן,
so too in words of Torah there is a "small day": Malchus, the mouth, the Oral Torah, a small light,
וְיֵשׁ יוֹם גָּדוֹל: בִּינָה, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא כָּלוּל בְּחָכְמָה,
and there is a "great day": Binah, which is also the Oral Torah as it is included within Chochmah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and as it is said
(ibid., v. 6):
כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה
"For Hashem gives wisdom"
תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב,
the Written Torah,
מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה
"from His mouth come knowledge and understanding (tevunah)"
בִּינָה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
Binah, the Oral Torah.
וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' נ"ג.):
עֵץ חַיִּים דָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא וְכוּלֵּי אֲמַאי אִיקְרֵי תּוֹרָה?
"Tree of life—this is the Torah, etc. Why is it called Torah?
בְּגִין דְּאוֹרֵי וְגַלֵּי בְּמַה דַּהֲוָה סָתִים
because it instructs and reveals that which was hidden"
וְהַיְינוּ יוֹם קָטָן, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
and this is the small day, the Oral Torah;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: חַיִּים — דְּכָל חַיִּים דִּלְעֵילָּא בַּהּ אִתְכְּלִילוּ וּמִינַּהּ נָפְקִין,
and afterward it says: "'Life'—because all supernal life is included within it and emerges from it,"
וְהַיְינוּ יוֹם גָּדוֹל שֶׁהוּא כְּאֶרֶז בַּלְּבָנוֹן יִשְׂגֶּה עַד עַתִּיקָא.
and this is the great day, which "grows tall like a cedar in Lebanon" reaching up to Atika.
וְכֵן בְּשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ שְׁנֵיהֶם:
And similarly on Shabbos both exist:
נְהוֹרָא לַהּ יְמַטֵּי, נְהוֹרָא יִשְׁרֵי בַּהּ
"Light reaches her, light rests upon her"
הַיְינוּ יוֹם קָטָן;
which is the small day;
וְיֵשׁ יוֹם גָּדוֹל: לְמֶחֱזֵי זִיו דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין, כְּשֶׁהִיא זִיוּוּג קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
and there is the great day: "to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin," when there is the union of the Holy One, blessed is He, and His Shechinah
וְזֶה מִצַּד הָאַהֲבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם אֲהַבְתָּנוּ ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ חוּקִּים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ
and this is from the aspect of love, as we say, "With an eternal love You have loved us, Hashem our God; statutes and judgments You have taught us"
שַׁבָּת קָטָן תְּשׁוּבָה תַּתָּאָה, שַׁבָּת גָּדוֹל תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה מִצַּד הַיִּרְאָה.
corresponding to Shabbos Katan (lower repentance) and Shabbos HaGadol (supernal repentance) from the aspect of fear.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And in the holy Zohar
(ibid. 54b):
שִׂימֵנִי כַחוֹתָם עַל לִבֶּךָ
"Place me as a seal upon your heart"
דָּא חוֹתָם שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין דְּאָנַח בַּר נָשׁ עַל לִבֵּיהּ.
this is the seal of Tefillin that a person places opposite his heart.
וְהַיְינוּ דִּתְפִילִּין יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת:
That is, Tefillin contain four Torah passages:
שְׁתֵּי פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת מֵאַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: וְאָהַבְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ וְגוֹמֵר לְאַהֲבָה אֶת ה',
two passages about Israel's love for the Holy One, blessed is He—"And you shall love, etc." and "And it shall be if you hearken, etc., to love Hashem"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁתַּיִם מִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁבָּא מִצַּד אַהֲבַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and afterward two passages about the Exodus from Egypt, which came from the Holy One, blessed is He's love for Knesses Yisrael,
וְזֶה מִתְּפִילִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא דְּמִשְׁתַּבַּח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
and this corresponds to the Tefillin of the Master of the Universe in which He praises Israel
(בְּרָכוֹת ו'.).
(Berachos 6a).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ח', ו'):
(Shir HaShirim 8:6):
כִּי עַזָּה כַמָּוֶת אַהֲבָה
"For love is as fierce as death"
אַהֲבַת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
the love between Hashem, may He be blessed, and Knesses Yisrael.
וּבְשַׁבָּת יְכוֹלִים לִזְכּוֹת לְשַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה וְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה, שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, יוֹם גָּדוֹל,
And on Shabbos one can merit both the Lower Shabbos and the Supernal Shabbos—Shabbos HaGadol, the Great Day
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין.
for through observing Shabbos, Israel are immediately redeemed.

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 160 — "Before the world was created... a great light was created, which no creature could master. The Holy One, blessed is He, foresaw that they could not bear it; He took one seventh and placed it for them in its stead, and the rest He hid away for the righteous in the future, saying: If they merit this seventh and guard it, I will give them this in the final world."

rich.text: Sefer HaBahir 160

— "Before the world was created... a great light was created, which no creature could master. The Holy One, blessed is He, foresaw that they could not bear it; He took one seventh and placed it for them in its stead, and the rest He hid away for the righteous in the future, saying: If they merit this seventh and guard it, I will give them this in the final world."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Vayechi — “It is known that the light the Holy One created on the first day He hid away for the righteous in the future. On all the weekdays the light and the holiness are clothed in many garments, and it is impossible to see them through the clothing; but when holy Shabbos comes, rest comes, and then the light hidden for the righteous is revealed to each person according to his level. The Gemara says that Shabbos is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; so each person has a crucible and touchstone to see his level in the World to Come: according to the holiness he has on holy Shabbos, sixty times that he will have in the World to Come.” Connection: Both hold that the hidden light of the first day shines on Shabbos and make it the one-sixtieth foretaste of the World to Come; Maor VaShemesh adds that the weekday light is only clothed, and that one's Shabbos holiness measures one's share in the World to Come.

rich.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Vayechi

— “It is known that the light the Holy One created on the first day He hid away for the righteous in the future. On all the weekdays the light and the holiness are clothed in many garments, and it is impossible to see them through the clothing; but when holy Shabbos comes, rest comes, and then the light hidden for the righteous is revealed to each person according to his level. The Gemara says that Shabbos is one-sixtieth of the World to Come; so each person has a crucible and touchstone to see his level in the World to Come: according to the holiness he has on holy Shabbos, sixty times that he will have in the World to Come.” Connection: Both hold that the hidden light of the first day shines on Shabbos and make it the one-sixtieth foretaste of the World to Come; Maor VaShemesh adds that the weekday light is only clothed, and that one's Shabbos holiness measures one's share in the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 25:12 — "Rabbi Levi said: If Israel kept Shabbos properly even one day, the son of David would come... as it says (Tehillim 95:7), 'Today (hayom), if you would heed His voice.'" Shocher Tov 95: "If Israel kept even one Shabbos as it should be kept, they would at once be redeemed, as it says, 'Today, if you would heed His voice,' and it is written, 'Keep the Shabbos day.'"

paragraphs.text: Berachos 57b — "Five things are one-sixtieth: fire, honey, Shabbos, sleep and a dream. Fire is one-sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey, one-sixtieth of the manna; Shabbos, one-sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep, one-sixtieth of death; a dream, one-sixtieth of prophecy." [Rashi does not comment on the Shabbos clause.]

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 54a (Metzora) — "'Behold, a day comes for Hashem' (Zecharyah 14:1): it should have said 'will come'... Rabbi Yitzchak said: There are two days to the Holy One, blessed is He: one that abides with Him, and one that comes before Him; and with these He wages war against all." The glosses Malchus and Binah are Rav Tzadok's.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 13 — “‘As in the days of your going out of Egypt I will show him wonders’: seven days of Pesach of the first exile and seven of the final exile. Just as at the Exodus there were seven days of Pesach from the side of the lower Shechinah, ‘small days,’ so in the future, when they are redeemed in Nisan, there will be seven days of Pesach of the final exile, and the redemption will be from the side of Binah, the ‘great day,’ as the Zohar says, ‘Two days are there for the Holy One.’ And it says ‘I will show him,’ in the hidden form, which is Binah, the upper world.” Connection: Both use “Two days are there for the Holy One” for a small day of Malchus and a great day of Binah; Pesach 13 applies it to the Pesach of Egypt and the Pesach of the final redemption.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 65a (Acharei Mos) — "Because she is called Mother, a female, gevurah and judgment issue from her. She is called mercy alone, yet from her side judgments are aroused; therefore [the Name] is written with the letters of mercy and vocalized as judgment." Rav Tzadok's reference reads "ibid. 64, end of amud a"; this is the passage that matches his words.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 5b (Hakdamah) — "Another Shabbos remained unmentioned and was ashamed... He said to her: My daughter, you are Shabbos... but I crown you with a higher crown.
